name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Nano (ESP32-S3R8, Arduino Nano ESP32 compatible)
radio: the SoC's own radios: wifi24, ble

flash.bootloader_instructions: Hold BOOT while plugging in USB-C; release after a second. The chip's USB-JTAG-serial port (303a:1001) appears and esptool can write it — this board does not need Arduino's DFU route.
flash.note: Waveshare documents it as 'select Arduino Nano ESP32' in the IDE: pinout and RGB LED pins follow the Nano ESP32, so kitsune's arduino-nano-esp32 builds are what this target flashes. Not yet flashed from this page.

usb.when: ESP32-S3 USB-JTAG-serial (download mode and, with CDC on boot, the running firmware)

led.note: three analog-driven LED lines (kitsune writes 255 - value, scaled to 75)

battery.divider_note: Powered from USB or a 5 V pack. kitsune's note: the pack must not have a low-current cut-off, or the board never wakes from deep sleep.

notes: A stand-in for the Arduino Nano ESP32 target without Arduino's DFU bootloader in the way.
Serial: native USB CDC; kitsune's arduino_nano_esp32 env sets ARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT, so its lines appear on the same port.
Power: kitsune foxes sleep between transmissions; a USB power bank with a low-current auto-off cuts power during the sleep and the fox never wakes (kitsune's README). Use a pack without auto-off.
Serial: native USB — the console port disappears while the chip sleeps and returns when it wakes (kitsune's README: 'Serial console during sleep: no'). 'serial port dropped' each cycle is expected.

circuitpython.note: CircuitPython has no Waveshare ESP32-S3-Nano build (checked 2026-10-24). The board is an Arduino Nano ESP32 clone (ESP32-S3R8, 16 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM, same pinout), so the Arduino Nano ESP32 build is what goes on it and the board reports itself as arduino_nano_esp32s3; the page maps that id back to this target. An actual Arduino Nano ESP32 running that build behaves the same way here. To verify on the board.
